newsitem.title: UK: Boots says Q1 Chemists sales up 5.1 pct.
newsitem.headline: Boots says Q1 Chemists sales up 5.1 pct.

text.p: British healthcare and general retailer Boots Co Plc said on Thursday that like for like sales at Boots the Chemists in the first quarter of the current year were up 5.1 percent on the same period last year.
It said in a statement that sales for the company as a whole increased by nearly 11 percent compared with the same period last year.

The poor weather in June hit UK sales of sun preparations and hay fever remedies but there were good levels of growth elsewhere at Boots the Chemists, chief executive Lord Blyth of Rowington said in a statement.

"Looking ahead, market conditions continue to be satisfactory for our businesses. We believe that we have strategies and people in place to continue the delivery of long term growth," he said in a statement to be presented to the annual meeting later on Thursday.
Sales at Boots Opticians were up 24 percent on a like for like basis in the first quarter.
Like for like sales at its 132 stores of DIY division Do It All edged up 2-1/2 percent, though early indications for this month show sales have improved along with the weather.

Chairman Sir Michael Angus said competition remains strong in the current year for Boots' business but consumer confidence is still there, "supported in part by the 'feel good factor' generated by windfall bonuses from the financial sector."
